findings.finding: No new auth surface, no schema/migration change, no data-exposure change. Numeric bounds (bedrooms Float min 0/max 20, bathrooms Int min 0/max 20) are identical before and after, enforced server-side via Zod .strict() schemas which remain the security boundary — client-side listingValidation.ts mirrors but does not replace them.
React renders the new numeric input's error messages and values as JSX text (auto-escaped), and the input is type=number/inputMode=numeric — no injection or XSS surface introduced.

Ownership checks, rate limiting (writeRateLimiter), and authenticate/optionalAuth gates on POST/PATCH/DELETE /listings are unchanged; the listingSchemas.ts extraction is a behavior-preserving refactor (confirmed by reading the full route file and diffing against the pre-task commit).
applyRangeFilters correctly preserves the pre-existing != null (not truthiness) check so a literal 0 filter value still applies — no filter-bypass regression for studio (0-bedroom) listings.

Could not execute the new Vitest suites in this sandbox (npm commands are denied by the environment's permission policy, matching what Backend/Frontend engineers reported). Verified correctness by manual code reading instead: schemas, bounds, and applyRangeFilters logic all trace correctly against Prisma types (bedrooms Float, bathrooms Int) and the pre-task behavior.
findings.recommendedAction: Run `npm test` in both rentals/backend and rentals/frontend in an environment with npm access before considering this fully verified; not a blocker for security sign-off since no security-relevant logic changed.
